extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers learning or using algebraic geometry (cohomology, base change, moduli)
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and applying theorems about cohomology of coherent sheaves in proper/flat families (semicontinuity, Grauert, cohomology-and-base-change) and using them to construct moduli spaces (Grassmannian, hypersurfaces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Theorem 26.2.1 (Mumford idea / finite free complex)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π : X → Spec B is a proper morphism, and F is a coherent sheaf on X, flat over Spec B, where B is Noetherian. Then there is a complex ... of finitely generated free B-modules and an isomorphism of functors Hp(K• ⊗B A) ∼→ Hp(X_A, F_A) for all p, for all ring maps B → A (here A needn’t be Noetherian).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces the ˇCech complex by a finite complex of free modules so cohomology questions become linear-algebraic (matrices over B). Use this to study base change by examining minors/ranks of the matrices; see the construction via Lemmas 26.2.2 and 26.2.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semicontinuity Theorem 26.1.1 (upper semicontinuity of cohomology dimensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a proper morphism π and F coherent and flat over the base, the function q ↦ dim_{κ(q)} Hp(X_q, F|_{X_q}) is upper semicontinuous on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by expressing Hp in terms of kernels and images of maps in the finite free complex K• and observing that ranks of images (given by minors) are lower semicontinuous, hence the dimensions are upper semicontinuous (see formula (26.2.4.1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grauert's Theorem 26.1.5 (local freeness and base-change when dimensions are constant)
rubrics_metrics.description: If hp(X_q, F|_{X_q}) is locally constant in q, then Rp^π_* F is locally free and its formation commutes with base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the finite free complex, local constancy forces the relevant δ maps to be strongly of constant rank; then ker/im/coker are locally free (Observation 26.2.8) and cohomology sheaves are locally free (see proof 26.2.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology and Base Change Theorem 26.1.6 (criteria for commuting and local-freeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part (i): surjectivity of the natural map φ^p_q : (R^p π_* F) ⊗ κ(q) → H^p(X_q, F|_{X_q}) implies formation of R^p π_* F commutes with base change near q. Part (ii): R^p π_* F is locally free near q if and only if the natural map H^{p-1}(X_q, F|_{X_q}) → (R^{p-1}π_* F) ⊗ κ(q) is surjective (equivalently, a condition on surjectivity at p−1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to the finite free complex K• and checking that surjectivity at the fiber is equivalent to δ_p being strongly of constant rank near q (Lemma 26.2.10 and Exercise 26.2.C); then ker δ_p is locally free and Hp(K•) commutes with base change (26.2.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: O-connected morphism
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism π : X → Y is O-connected if the natural map O_Y → π_* O_X is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: O-connectedness is local on the target and preserved by composition; for proper morphisms Zariski’s Connectedness Lemma shows proper O-connected morphisms of locally Noetherian schemes have connected fibers. The class is preserved by flat base change (use cohomology commuting with flat base change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion (Exercise 26.1.H): h^0 = 1 on fibers ⇒ O-connected
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is proper and flat with locally Noetherian schemes and the fibers satisfy h^0(X_q, O_{X_q}) = 1 for all q, then π is O-connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Cohomology and Base Change: the map O_Y ⊗ κ(q) → H^0(X_q, O_{X_q}) ∼= κ(q) is surjective, hence an isomorphism by the theorem; then π_* O_X is locally free of rank 1 and Nakayama-type arguments show the pushforward map is an isomorphism globally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 26.1.11 (descent of line bundles along proper O-connected morphisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is flat, proper, with geometrically connected and geometrically reduced fibers (hence O-connected), Y reduced, and L an invertible sheaf on X trivial on every fiber, then π_* L is locally free of rank 1 (call it M) and the natural map π^* M → L is an isomorphism (i.e., L descends to an invertible sheaf M on Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Grauert’s Theorem to identify fiberwise H^0 with κ(q) and show π_* L is invertible; surjectivity on fibers gives surjectivity of π^* π_* L → L, and Nakayama’s Lemma implies it is an isomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 26.2.7: strongly of constant rank (for morphisms of vector bundles)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism φ : E → F of finite-rank locally free sheaves is strongly of constant rank a if locally there are trivializations E|_U ≅ O_U^{a+b}, F|_U ≅ O_U^{a+c} in which φ is the projection/inclusion onto the first a summands (i.e., locally isomorphic to diag(I_a,0)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notion commutes with base change. When φ is strongly of constant rank, ker φ, im φ, and coker φ are locally free and their constructions commute with base change (Observation 26.2.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence criteria for 'strongly of constant rank' (Exercises 26.2.A, 26.2.B, 26.2.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: φ is strongly of constant rank a iff (A) coker φ is locally free of rank a; (B) if X is reduced then φ is strongly of constant rank a iff the fiberwise ranks satisfy rank(φ|_p)=a for all p ∈ X; (C) φ is strongly constant near p iff the natural map (ker φ)|_p → ker(φ|_p) is surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these equivalences to check strong constancy via fiberwise rank computations, cokernel freeness, or surjectivity on stalks; Exercise hints reference Exercise 14.3.L and 14.2.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mumford's strategy (methodological guideline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Turn questions about pushforwards and their behavior under base change into linear algebra questions by replacing the ˇCech complex with a finite complex of free modules (K•) that computes cohomology and behaves well under base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This idea underpins proofs of Semicontinuity, Grauert, and Cohomology-and-Base-Change: analyse ranks of matrices representing differentials, use minors to detect locus where ranks drop, and deduce (semi)continuity and local-freeness results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 26.2.2 (construction of finite free complex quasiisomorphic to given complex)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a complex C• of B-modules with Hi(C•) finitely generated and bounded above (Cp=0 for p>n) and B Noetherian, there exists a complex K• of finite-rank free B-modules (Kp=0 for p>n) and a morphism α : K• → C• inducing isomorphisms Hi(K•) ∼→ Hi(C•) for all i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof proceeds inductively by choosing generators of cohomology and lifting them; Noetherian hypotheses ensure finite generation of kernels used in the construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 26.2.3 (quasiisomorphism commutes with arbitrary base change)
rubrics_metrics.description: If α : K• → C• is a quasiisomorphism of complexes of flat B-modules bounded on the right, then for every B-algebra A the map α ⊗_B A : K• ⊗_B A → C• ⊗_B A is also a quasiisomorphism (i.e., the quasiisomorphism commutes with arbitrary change of base ring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mapping-cone exactness and flatness to show the mapping cone remains exact after tensoring, concluding cohomology is preserved under base change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 26.2.10 (surjectivity criterion via mapping cone / Snake Lemma)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a map of complexes with the left vertical arrow surjective, Hp(K•) → Hp(J•) is surjective iff ker δ_p^K → ker δ_p^J is surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Snake Lemma on the diagram relating im δ_{p-1}, ker δ_p and cohomology to translate surjectivity statements between complexes to surjectivity on kernels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application: Grassmannian representability via cohomology-and-base-change
rubrics_metrics.description: To show families of linearly embedded P^{k-1}'s in P^{n-1}_B are represented by G(k,n), use the short exact sequence 0 → I_X(1) → O_{P^{n-1}_B}(1) → O_X(1) → 0 and Cohomology-and-Base-Change to get R^iπ_* O_X(1)=0 for i>0 and π_* O_X(1) locally free of rank k; the surjection O_B^{⊕ n} → π_* O_X(1) gives the corresponding point of the Grassmannian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify vanishing of higher cohomology on fibers and apply the Cohomology-and-Base-Change Theorem (26.1.6) to promote fiberwise statements to locally free pushforwards that glue to give the universal quotient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application: parametrizing degree-d hypersurfaces (Proposition 26.3.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree d hypersurfaces in P^n are parametrized by P^{(n+d choose d)-1} by considering the exact sequence 0 → I_X(d) → O_{P^n_B}(d) → O_X(d) → 0 and using cohomology-and-base-change to show higher pushforwards vanish and π_* I_X(d) is a line bundle (equation of X); dualizing yields a morphism B → P^{...}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret π_* O_{P^n_B}(d) as the free sheaf of homogeneous polynomials of degree d and π_* I_X(d) as the line bundle of equations; duals give the desired morphism to projective parameter space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removing Noetherian hypotheses (26.2.12) and necessity of finite presentation (26.2.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Noetherian hypotheses in the cohomology/base-change theorems can often be replaced by finite-presentation hypotheses (via spreading out to Spec Z[x_1,...,x_N]/I), but finite-presentation conditions are necessary: without them one can find flat/projective examples where fiber dimensions or arithmetic genus jump.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To extend results, produce a base change diagram to a finitely presented model over a Noetherian ring (Exercise 26.2.E) and apply the Noetherian statements there; be aware of explicit counterexamples showing the necessity of finite-presentation hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hodge bundle (Exercise 26.1.N)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is a flat proper morphism whose fibers are regular irreducible curves of genus g, then Ω_{X/Y} is a line bundle on X and π_* Ω_{X/Y} is a locally free sheaf on Y of rank g (the Hodge bundle), and its formation commutes with base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Cohomology-and-Base-Change twice (for p=2 and p=1) to check local-freeness and base-change compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension formula for cohomology via finite-free complex (26.2.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For q ∈ Y, dim_{κ(q)} H^p(X_q, F|_{X_q}) = dim_{κ(q)} ker(δ_p ⊗ κ(q)) - dim_{κ(q)} im(δ_{p-1} ⊗ κ(q)) - dim_{κ(q)} im(δ_p ⊗ κ(q)) (as arranged in (26.2.4.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit expression shows cohomology dimensions are built from ranks of kernels and images of the differentials of K•, allowing semicontinuity arguments by studying where ranks drop via vanishing of minors.
